I am 71 this year. I have worked my 5 mu of land in Quzhou for 55 years. I only finished primary school, so I do not read farming books. My father taught me, and after that I learned by watching my neighbors. If Lao Wang does something and his field looks good, I do the same. I have 4 mu where I grow winter wheat and then summer maize back to back, and 1 mu I keep for cotton. There are only two of us at home now, so I cannot manage more — hiring labor costs too much, and I would rather spend that money on fertilizer.

For the wheat already in the ground from last October, I will manage it just like last year. Before sowing I ploughed the field and put down one 50-jin bag of compound fertilizer per mu. At green-up in March I will spread half a bag of urea on each mu. I do not weigh out kilograms — I measure in bags — but that is about 18 jin of nitrogen per mu. I will irrigate three times: the winter water, once at jointing, and once more in April if the sky stays dry. I will spray twice, once for weeds and once for aphids if I see them. Last year I got about 900 jin per mu, and I expect the same.

For maize, after I cut the wheat in June I will rotary till the stubble right away and plant hybrid seed — Zhengdan 958, the one in the yellow bag. I will put one bag of compound fertilizer per mu in the rows at planting, and when the maize is knee-high I will top-dress with half a bag of urea. That is about 17 jin of nitrogen per mu. I will irrigate two times, three if the drought is bad. I will spray twice: herbicide once, insecticide once. I expect about 1,100 jin per mu.

For cotton on the 1 mu, I will plant hybrid seed in late April. Cotton needs more potassium or the bolls drop off. I will use one bag of compound fertilizer per mu, plus an extra 30 jin of potassium fertilizer, and some urea on top. I will irrigate three times in summer. I will spray four times for bollworm and whitefly. Picking is hard on an old man’s back, but the price is okay. I expect 500 to 600 jin of seed cotton per mu.

I do not like to change what works. Fertilizer is expensive — every yuan is real money. But I would rather put a little too much than too little. A bad harvest is a disaster; wasting some fertilizer is just a cost. When I am unsure, I do what I did last year. I watch what my neighbors do. If everyone around me applies one bag, I apply one bag. That is how I decide.
